methodology.selection: activity.json kind=assessment, with content.json and capture-complete.json
methodology.question_unit: One finalized content.questions item per account/task/question; attempts are not appended.
methodology.source_identity: Explicit permanent q-ID and numeric topic/KP links from result HTML, cross-checked against saved metadata and the on-disk history fragment.
methodology.kp_identity_caveat: raw_kp_anchor_id is the source /topics/{topic}#{anchor} fragment. It is not automatically an EDB knowledge-point/id or a canonical-example ID.
methodology.order: Question order is the quiz result-header question number, not the KP position within its lesson.
methodology.topic_labels: The result header labels the KP, not the topic; missing topic titles remain null until an authoritative identity join.
methodology.missing_attempts: Final result history includes unanswered questions; these are retained in the assessment sample.
methodology.deduplication: Report duplicate task and permanent question IDs explicitly; never merge different assessment occurrences silently.

questions.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-3)^{n-1}}{n}{x}^{n}.
$$

Calculate the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor series expansion about $x=0$ of ${f}^{′}(x).$

questions.kp_title: Finding the Total Change of a Function Given Its Rate of Change
questions.problem:
The rate at which packages arrive at a warehouse one morning is given by the function

$$
r(t)=50-4t,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in packages per hour and $t>0$ is the time in hours since $6\,\text{a.m}.$
Packages are also being shipped out at a steady rate of $10$ packages per hour.

If there were $300$ packages in the warehouse at $6\,\text{a.m},$ how many packages will be there at $11\,\text{a.m}?$

There will be 
{{field-1}}  packages in the warehouse at $11\,\text{a.m}.$

questions.kp_title: Identifying the Point of Fastest Increase of a Logistic Growth Model
questions.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of owls in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=6P-0.001\,5{P}^{2},\,P(0)=400,
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in years. For which value of $P$ is the owl population growing at the fastest possible rate?
